title: Carabao Cup second-round draw: Chelsea vs Luton, Tottenham vs Charlton, Newcastle vs West Brom
description: Four-time winners Nottingham Forest will face Leeds in the Carabao Cup in the only all-Premier League tie in the second round of the competition. Chel
body: Four-time winners Nottingham Forest will face Leeds in the Carabao Cup in the only all-Premier League tie in the second round of the competition. Chelsea, who have won the competition five times, will welcome League One Luton to Stamford Bridge, while Tottenham will host Championship side Charlton. David Moyes will return to Deepdale as Everton visit Preston North End, where he began his managerial career.Meanwhile, Newcastle will take on second-tier West Brom and Fulham will play AFC Wimbledon at Craven Cottage. Brentford have a potentially tricky away trip to Birmingham City while Ipswich will play League One Leicester.Also in the southern section West Ham, who beat Portsmouth in Saturday's first round, travel to fellow Championship side Southampton.The draw for the second round of the EFL Cup was split across northern and southern sections.All matches are due to take place in the midweek of the week commencing Monday, 24 August.The nine English clubs involved in Europe this season will enter the competition in the third round.After Sky Sports chose Fulham v Chelsea for live Premier League broadcast on Monday, 24 August, the potential for a knock-on impact was clear. With the two teams not in Europe, and thus entering the Carabao Cup in the second round, both faced playing two games in the midweek.Ordinarily, that should mean the EFL Cup ties would be played on the Thursday, with 72 hours' rest.That, too, would impact the Premier League's weekend schedule. Fulham's match at Sunderland, which was not selected for TV broadcast, was switched to the Sunday. Chelsea v Brighton, meanwhile, was chosen by Sky for the Sunday.All good so far.That was until both Fulham and Chelsea were drawn at home in the Carabao Cup - and they are not supposed to play at home on the same day. The police will have to make a concession, or the EFL will have to get creative.But there is another knock-on effect - at very short notice for eight EFL clubs.The opponents of Fulham and Chelsea - Wimbledon and Luton respectively - are in League One action on the Saturday after the ties.If one or both Carabao Cup ties are scheduled for the Thursday, then the Saturday games would ordinarily move to the Sunday.And there's another complication.The following Tuesday there is a full programme of League One games - and that could impact a further four matches with the potential they might have to move to Wednesday. Either teams will have to play two games within 48 hours, or supporters who have made travel arrangements are going to find games displaced.The games potentially impacted are as follows.Saturday, 29 AugustWimbledon v WiganMansfield v LutonTuesday, 1 SeptemberBurton v WimbledonWigan v MK DonsLuton v StockportReading v Mansfield

title: 30 years later, a former rival will stand trial for Tupac's murder
description: It's been three decades filled with mystery, conspiracies - and anger.The drive-by shooting that killed rap superstar Tupac Shakur on 7 September 1996
body: It's been three decades filled with mystery, conspiracies - and anger.The drive-by shooting that killed rap superstar Tupac Shakur on 7 September 1996 changed the trajectory of hip-hop and elevated the rapper from the face of the genre to a cultural icon.His killing became one of popular culture's great mysteries, with countless theories but no arrests until 2023, when Duane "Keffe D" Davis was unexpectedly charged with murdering the famous rapper.The 63-year-old former gang boss is due to stand trial in Las Vegas, where he is accused of murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang. He's pleaded not guilty. If convicted, he faces life in prison without parole.The trial is likely to unravel the intricacies of the bitter and deadly East Coast vs West Coast rap rivalries and turf wars between the Bloods and the Crips street gangs that were immortalised in rap lyrics and news reports in the 1990s.It could also include several celebrity witnesses - including Suge Knight, the former CEO of Death Row Records, who has been thought of as the last surviving witness to Shakur's death.But the complicated case hinges almost exclusively on one key piece of evidence: a book co-authored by Davis that he has argued is partially a piece of fiction.Jury selection in the case began on Monday, with opening arguments due to start on 17 August.To understand how the case became so mythologised, you have to go back to rivalries that grew larger than the men at its centre.In the Los Angeles gang landscape of the 1990s, there was a vicious turf war between the Bloods, often represented by the colour red, and Crips, who often wore blue. But that territorial dispute spread through the airwaves as part of a bigger national rivalry - East Coast v West Coast rap. The genre dispute was represented by two rival record companies that defined 1990s hip-hop: Knight's Death Row Records and Sean "Diddy" Combs' Bad Boy Records. "The funny thing about it is Tupac is actually an East Coast rapper," said Jeff Pearlman, author of Only God Can Judge Me: The Many Lives of Tupac Shakur.Born in New York City, Tupac moved to northern California as a teenager. He became known as a southern California rapper after signing with Death Row Records, which included acts like Snoop Dogg and Dr Dre.Santi Elijah Holley, author of An Amerikan Family: The Shakurs and the Nation They Created, says the Death Row persona never told the whole story.Tupac's mother Afeni was a Black Panther and he grew up around the black liberation movement. Holley says his music became his politics: "His activism was his art, his lyrics."He acted in a number of Hollywood movies, and released hip-hop's first double album, All Eyez on Me, which sold over 5,000,000 copies. That album, which debuted months before his death, cemented his place in the cannon of gangsta rap, a genre that celebrated the violent life of street criminals and drug dealers.After he was shot in Las Vegas on 7 September 1996, he became immortalised as a kind of martyr for the lifestyle he helped make famous.That fatal night began when Tupac and Knight attended a boxing match between Mike Tyson and Bruce Seldon at the MGM Grand.After the match, surveillance footage captured Tupac and members of his entourage, who police have said were associated the Mob Piru Bloods street gang, attacking a man named Orlando Anderson, an alleged member of the South Side Compton Crips.About three hours after the attack, Tupac was riding in the passenger seat of Knight's BMW driving through Las Vegas when a white Cadillac pulled alongside them and opened fire.Tupac was hit four times and died six days later.For nearly three decades, the killing remained one of America's most famous unsolved murders. There is no single explanation why.Las Vegas police have long said witnesses refused to co-operate. Members of Tupac's entourage said police initially treated them like suspects and failed to follow important leads.Within weeks of the shooting, investigators had identified Anderson from the MGM footage and questioned him.He denied involvement and was never charged; he was killed in an unrelated shooting in 1998.Over the years, police say they pursued thousands of tips, but the case stalled amid disappearing witnesses, many of whom were also killed in gang-related shootings, limited physical evidence, and a street code that forbade co-operation with police.It was years later when Anderson's uncle, Davis, started talking and according to police, blew the case wide open again.It was ultimately the death of another legendary rapper that helped unravel Tupac's shooting death.Months after Shakur was gunned down, Biggie Smalls, or the Notorious BIG, was killed in a drive-by shooting in Los Angeles.Both rappers were the stars of their respective rival record labels - Shakur with Death Row Records and Biggie with Bad Boy Records.Biggie's case has remained unsolved, with no arrests or suspects.In the mid 2000s the Los Angeles Police Department reopened the investigation and spoke with Davis, who was at a party with Biggie before the fatal shooting. While Davis said he didn't have information about Biggie's death, he did have knowledge of Tupac's case and shared that he was in the car when the rapper was shot and killed. He told police the information in exchange that he not be charged.That deal stuck until years later, when Davis went public with his knowledge.He co-authored a memoir in 2019 titled Compton Street Legend, that claimed he not only was inside the vehicle when Tupac was shot, but he was also the person who "tossed" the gun used to kill him into the backseat of the Cadillac. He never claimed to be the person who opened fire.Davis also elaborated on the shooting to the media, detailing information to reporters in interviews.Las Vegas police said his public statements had "reinvigorated" the investigation. Over the next couple of years they spent time corroborating Davis' account and then in 2023, searched his home and seized multiple computers, two tubs of photographs and a slew of Tupac-related material, including a Vibe magazine.He was arrested later that year.Prosecutors have alleged that Tupac's killing was in retaliation for the beating of Davis' nephew - Orlando Anderson - just hours before the shooting.They claim that Davis was the architect of the crime, who ordered the shooting and supplied the deadly weapon to further gang criminal conduct.Listen to Fame Under Fire: The Tupac Murder TrialNevada prosecutors argued that by publicly talking about what happened on the night of Tupac's death and writing a book where he claimed to have supplied the gun, Davis had broken the agreement he entered into with law enforcement. A judge later sided with the prosecutor's argument, opening the door for Davis' arrest.Davis and his defence team have argued that the book was co-authored and sections were embellished or fictionalised to make a profit, and they should not be viewed as direct admissions. In an interview last week with a local TV news station, Davis denied being in Las Vegas when Tupac was killed and distanced himself from the memoir that lists him as an author."I did not write that book," Davis told Fox 5. "A ghost writer wrote that."He also said he might take the stand and testify at his trial. "If I have to, I will."Trial attorney Shaun Kent told the BBC: "This is what makes this case so fascinating. The two biggest pieces of evidence against Keffe D came from Keffe D."Keffe D has the right to take the stand and say 'I made all this up. I lied to sell copies of the book. I lied to the police. I'm a liar but I did not murder Tupac.'"Davis has also publicly stated multiple times that Bad Boy Records head Sean "Diddy" Combs had offered him $1m to kill Death Row Records rivals Tupac and Knight.

title: The lonely Chinese men being conned by fake brides
description: Figure caption, Watch: Chinese man targeted by 'flash wedding' scamsByLaura BickerChina correspondent Reporting fromBeijing and GuiyangAt 37, Wang Zhu
body: Figure caption, Watch: Chinese man targeted by 'flash wedding' scamsByLaura BickerChina correspondent Reporting fromBeijing and GuiyangAt 37, Wang Zhuang had almost given up hope of finding a wife, until he saw the glossy matchmaking adverts.They promised he wouldn't have to waste years on building a relationship that had no future. They offered to introduce him to a demure, devoted woman."The matchmakers said that girls from Guizhou are frugal," Wang says. "They told me they are good at running a household, able to do housework, and their families are very poor, so after marrying into your family, they would settle down and live a life with you."So Wang travelled to Guiyang, a city in the southwestern province of Guizhou, in the hope of finding his soulmate.He thought he had, when he was matched with a woman who seemed to tick every box. They had only met a few times before they married.Then, almost as quickly as his new life had begun, it was over."My whole family has been thrown into chaos," he says, shaking his head.He is still picking up the pieces more than a year after he discovered that everything he had been told by his wife was a lie.She was a former karaoke hostess who'd been married three times, had three children, a serious sexually transmitted disease and was deeply in debt. She had even lied about her age.He is fighting for a divorce and cannot return home to his old life - at least until he can recoup some of his life savings, which he says he paid to the agency within hours of being introduced to several potential matches."My parents blame me. I have insomnia and anxiety. I can't focus on work."Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Chinese brides are in huge demand because of a steep gender imbalanceWang's story is an extreme symptom of a demographic crisis that has long been in the making in China.For decades, China's Communist Party decreed that couples could have only one child. They reversed course in January 2016 but by then the "one-child" policy, coupled with a preference for boys, had produced a shrinking pool of women and a stark gender imbalance.There are now 30 million more men than women in China – that's more than the male population of the UK, or the entire population of Australia.This has left men like Wang, who are in their late 30s and who live in smaller cities or far- flung, rural areas, with few options. Women in these places can afford to be choosy as they know they are in demand."The requirements for men are very high in my city. You need to have a car, a house and your family should preferably run a business," he says.Many families also demand a high "bride price", a longstanding Chinese custom where the groom's family gives money to the bride. In parts of China, where men far outnumber women, this has become a significant financial burden.Hence the appeal of matchmaking agencies like the ones in Guizhou, which are proposing a one-stop, quick solution - or "flash marriages".Matchmaking agencies are hardly new in China, but many seem to be finding vulnerable targets in men who are struggling to find partners as they grow older.So much so that state media recently reported that the industry had seen "rapid growth" which  had "bred illegal practices and chaos".Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The "flash marriage" market is now on Beijing's radarIt's hard to determine the scale of such fraud across China but it has grown enough to draw the attention of Chinese officials. Between January 2024 and March 2025, prosecutors handled cases involving 1,546 individuals for crimes related to the matchmaking industry.This month, five separate authorities jointly launched a nationwide crackdown on the matchmaking industry after the issue generated "widespread public concern".In one case, a matchmaking agency reportedly used karaoke waitresses as bait to defraud 128 victims of more than 2.5 million yuan (£274,000, $371,000)."I think the government could introduce industry-specific regulations targeting flash marriage scams," Fan Binghe from the Nanjing Office of the Beijing Jingshi law firm, told the BBC.Although Guiyang has become synonymous with this booming "flash marriage" market, there is little to suggest it is a romantic hub.The agency offices sit in a dense warren of buildings above a shopping precinct, where vendors sell local fruit and workers queue for takeaway sour soup rice noodles.Wang, however, was convinced he could trust them after the company told him they would do a full background check and that he would be entitled to compensation if he was the victim of fraud.So he paid up and the introductions began.Image caption, Wang was drawn to Guiyang by the promise of a demure spouse He met seven women in various "blind date" rooms over a few days while being carefully supervised by agency staff. He asked questions about where they came from, if they'd been married before and if they had any kids.He set his heart on the eighth woman he met. He was hoping to meet someone who hadn't been married before, with no children and who was just a little younger than him."She also dressed very simply," he recalls. "She looked introverted and honest."They met four or five times for just eight to ten minutes each time. He says they had been under strict instructions not to exchange phone numbers or any details on private messages, or they would be fined.After two or three days he decided she was the one and he agreed to pay her a substantial bride price. "I spent more than 300,000 yuan ($44,000)," he says, with a pile of well-thumbed legal papers in hand to prove it."If you include the wedding banquet and everything else, I spent around 400,000 to 500,00 yuan."The whole process was documented by the matchmaking agency in a series of glossy photos, which they also use to advertise their services on Chinese social media. In the video the couple are holding hands on a red carpet and smiling while romantic music plays in the background.Image caption, Wang with his ex-wife in a photo taken soon after their wedding  Just months into the marriage, debt collectors started calling, alleging she owed them money.Wang grew suspicious and wanted to know what else she had kept hidden. He checked her phone and found details of her former life, her birth certificate and former marriage documents.When he confronted her, she offered him a divorce, but refused to return a single penny of the bride price.He says he tried to hunt down the agency responsible for his marriage, but when he returned to their offices, they had packed up and disappeared.From his rented flat in Guiyang, just across from the main district which houses most of these agencies, Wang now spends his time making social media videos trying to warn other men about what can go wrong.In Guiyang, it is difficult to find an agency where the staff is willing to talk. One agency boss agreed to talk to us in their offices – although his business partner later asked us to leave.Inside there was a red carpet littered with fake petals ready for a proposal. He told us a couple had pledged to marry just hours before we arrived."There's a huge market for flash marriages in China. It only really emerged over the last two or three years," he told us.The agencies claim families here did not strictly adhere to the one-child policy, which means the area has a larger pool of women. "Even if a family had two or three daughters, they would keep trying for a son," one of them told the BBC.They say they are now trying to match these women with men from central provinces – like Wang who lives in Hebei – who are relatively wealthy but have few women around them."Our clients are free to choose whoever they like. The purpose of our business is to help people find someone they genuinely want to be with."One of the advertisements assures their prospective clients that "Three days with the right introduction can beat three years of dating".Image caption, It was in a room like this where Wang met his brideWang now spends his time trying to help other victims of similar spiels.His rented flat is full of men who are either searching for the owners of the agency who scammed them, or are trying to recoup their losses from their wives who ran off after only a few weeks of marriage.On a fold-up bed by the window, 59-year-old Xu Rulin from Jiangxi province pulls his carefully collated evidence out of a red plastic shopping bag.He spent nearly 500,000 yuan trying to find his son a wife through a "flash marriage" agency.Together they travelled to Guiyang - over 1000km away - and his son wed just seven days after he first met his bride in a "blind date" room.Xu says after the marriage was registered, she demanded they buy her an iPhone and transfer around 20,000 yuan to help her with her business. She also asked for 120,000 yuan for a wedding dress and jewellery, he claims."All I wanted was for her to genuinely settle down and live with us," he told us. "She said she wanted a house and I agreed to buy one for them. It was all agreed.But he says she ran away after living with them for less than two weeks. She has been detained by the police, and the couple have been able to get divorced.He says the owners of the matchmaking company were also arrested in January this year, but he is still in Guiyang trying to recover some of the losses.Image caption, The bride Xu Rulin spent a fortune finding for his son ran away within two weeksThe agency manager the BBC spoke to admitted there are no formal background checks on their clients."The women are introduced by local matchmakers who already know them very well. They know their family background because they're often from the same village. The male's matchmaker also usually knows the man very well."They would not say how much their services cost because that information was "confidential".He did say that if the information provided by either side is not truthful, then the client is entitled to get their money back."I'd say more than 90% of what our clients tell us here is true," he claimed."We have a saying here in China. One rotten mouse dropping spoils the whole pot of soup. That's exactly what it's like. We regularly attend meetings with the local police. If a matchmaking agency is found to be involved in marriage fraud, it will be held legally responsible."Image caption, This matchmaker says most people in the industry are genuineThis brings little comfort for those who have lost whatever money they had saved."I never imagined that with the agency charging such a high service fee, a local matchmaker in her hometown checking her background and the company offering so many guarantees, that the women's information would turn out to be completely fake," Wang says.He is almost resigned now to his losses. And he blames himself for falling for the scam: "Only women with problems would agree to these kind of flash marriages."He has kneeled at the police offices in Guiyang pleading for them to help him get his money back and he has even travelled to Beijing to urge the authorities to do more to combat this type of crime.These cases are difficult to prosecute, says Fan Binghe, the lawyer who has handled many.For one, Chinese law has no specific criminal offence which covers this kind of marriage fraud, and so to bring criminal charges, a victim has to establish that the aim of their spouse was always to take their money."In cases I've handled, suspects often argue that they genuinely intended to marry and live a good life but realised they were incompatible, had conflicts, and decided to end the relationship," he says."In situations like that, the line becomes blurred. Relationship issues are difficult to disprove."Image caption, Wang's apartment has turned into a refuge for scammed menEven harder is getting money back from sham matchmaking agencies which often shut up shop as soon as they have made enough cash.Wang has managed to get some money back, but not all."After going through something like this, I don't even know if I can still get married. It was already hard for me to find someone. And now I've spent so much money. I won't consider it now."Wang's life, and the life of the men in the apartment, all appear to be in limbo."It has taken almost two years, and even now I still don't know when I can divorce her," he says, surrounded by his legal paperwork."I don't know when this will be resolved, so I can restart a normal life. It feels endless."

title: The transgender controversy surrounding the WNBA
description: Last month, Cunningham, one of the league's most high-profile players, gave an interview to ESPN, external in which the conversation turned to the top
body: Last month, Cunningham, one of the league's most high-profile players, gave an interview to ESPN, external in which the conversation turned to the topic of "protecting" women's sports.The Indiana Fever guard said she had received criticism from people who believed she "hated" transgender people, something she denied.She said she wanted to "extend love" to everyone, but added: "I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."She later doubled down on her comments, saying it was "common sense", external to bar transgender athletes from competing in women's sports.Her words quickly moved beyond basketball and into a wider political debate in the United States.President Donald Trump expressed his support for Cunningham, while vice-president JD Vance said she was "inspiring".Though the 29-year-old later said she is "not a very political person", her remarks have followed her around the country. Competing rallies from critics and supporters were organised at Indiana's games, along with small-scale protests.The scale of the debate in the media, online and in politics was striking given no openly transgender woman is due to play, or has ever played, in the WNBA.The WNBA operates under a collective bargaining agreement (CBA), a deal negotiated between the league and its players association (WNBPA), setting rules on matters including player salary caps, revenue sharing, benefits and overall league operations.On player eligibility, the CBA states: "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA."The WNBA has yet to comment publicly on the row since Cunningham's comments but league commissioner Cathy Engelbert reportedly sent a memo to teams last week in which she said the matter would be discussed at an upcoming pre-arranged meeting with team presidents.In the memo, seen by the Associated Press, external, Engelbert said the league would "always approach this topic thoughtfully, respectfully, and in alignment with the longstanding values of our league".She added: "Our player eligibility rules, unlike the eligibility rules of some other leagues and governing bodies, are collectively bargained. Preserving the integrity of our game and ensuring fair competition will always remain among the league's highest priorities."However, the lack of detail in the league's eligibility criteria has been brought to light by Kanter Freedom, who finished his playing career with the Boston Celtics in 2022."If simply declaring who you are is all that's required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA," he wrote on Instagram, external.Kanter Freedom, who has previously spoken out about human rights violations in China and Turkey, among other issues, added: "I know my presence on the court will stir up strong opinions. I am definitely not here to mock, make fun of, or disrespect any community or personal choices."I'm simply asking that the current rules be applied equally to everyone - the rules that represent the very values many WNBA players and coaches have publicly advocated for."A day after Kanter Freedom's 'announcement', Royce White - who made three appearances in the NBA as a player and is now a Republican Senate candidate - said he would also declare for the Draft, adding: "I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball."Whether the vagueness of the rules are by design to leave it open to transgender women or a sign of an oversight that genuinely needs tightening up is not clear.BBC Sport has contacted Cunningham's representatives, the WNBA and WNBPA for comment.Cunningham's comments have become a flashpoint inside a league which has a long history of player activism on issues including race, gender equality and LGBTQ+ rights.The players' association did not mention Cunningham by name when it eventually addressed the debate.In a statement the WNBPA denounced "hate abuse and demonisation of the transgender community" and reaffirmed its commitment to "justice, equity, diversity and inclusion".It called on fans to report abusive behaviour at games and added that it would continue to have "hard" conversations but it "will not be used as political pawns".There is strong feeling on both sides of the argument. Minnesota Lynx head coach and president Cheryl Reeve, who said: "I come from a space of inclusion."The narrative that I think is problematic is to suggest that transgender athletes are the biggest problem in women's sports."Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" T-shirt before Minnesota played Indiana earlier this month and was seen speaking to Cunningham on court before the game.Cunningham later said the pair had exchanged their perspectives and that the conversation ended with "love and respect".Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams said she would welcome a transgender athlete "on my team or against my team, any time".Last month, the WNBA suspended Seattle Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton from attending the team's next five home games after an exchange with two fans, who were sat courtside displaying signs thanking Cunningham for "speaking up for girls".Keaton reportedly confronted the teenage fans and admonished them during the game. The Storm have since apologised.As for Cunningham, the attention has increasingly become an unwelcome distraction.Having defended her original comments, she said recently that she now wanted the conversation to return to what was happening on court."I want to get back to basketball, it's always been about basketball" she said, arguing that the standard of play in the WNBA was being overshadowed by issues away from the game.But that may prove difficult, as pressure grows on the league to clarify exactly who is eligible to play.In recent years, many governing bodies in sport have amended their rules about the inclusion of transgender athletes at the elite level, moving more towards restrictions.Athletics, cycling and aquatics, for example, have implemented outright bans on transgender women taking part in women's events.In March, it was announced that the women's category of Olympic sports will be limited to biological females from the LA Olympic Games in 2028.The International Olympic Committee (IOC) says eligibility will be determined by a "once-in-a-lifetime" sex test, which would prevent transgender women and those with differences in sexual development (DSD) who have gone through male puberty from competing.In the United States, transgender women and girls are banned from competing in women's sports categories in schools, universities and the grassroots level.That was part of an executive order - titled "Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports" - signed by President Trump last year. It does not cover professional sport.

title: Arsenal transfer news: Who are Gunners like to sign this transfer window?
description: For Arsenal it is hard to find any winger who would bring the excitement levels as well as the elite numbers that Vinicius Jr can.So what other option
body: For Arsenal it is hard to find any winger who would bring the excitement levels as well as the elite numbers that Vinicius Jr can.So what other options do the club and sporting director Andrea Berta have?Arsenal have come into this window looking at bringing in one or two forwards and Arteta has made it clearthat  any player that comes in this season has to take the club to the next level.Arsenal signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge to replace the outgoing Leandro Trossard, with the 24-year-old producing a remarkable 22 goals and 29 assists in all competitions last season for the Belgian club.Replicating those numbers is unlikely but the Greek international has looked one of the brightest players during pre-season.Arsenal have explored a move for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola, but Liverpool are also interested and the French side are demanding a fee of more than £100m for the forward.Morgan Rogers, before he completed his move to Chelsea from Aston Villa for £117m, was a target but Arsenal were not willing to go above £80m for the England international.Finding value in the market is hard and Berta is always looking to ensure that a deal represents value for the club.Kenan Yildiz is one player from Europe who is on Arsenal's list in a hunt for a left winger.The 21-year-old had a seriously impressive 2025-26 season for Juventus, scoring 11 goals and registering 10 assists in 47 appearances in all competitions.The Turkey international can play across the frontline too which adds another dynamic, which may make him appealing to Arteta.Like all good wingers he is unpredictable and can go on either the inside or outside, which means it is hard for defenders to know if he is going to cross the ball or shoot.And stats from Opta show that, of all players in Europe's top five leagues last season, only Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes (98) and Werder Bremen's Romano Schmid (77) created more open-play chances than Yildiz, while it was only Vinicius (43) who created more chances after carrying the ball than Yildiz too (37).However, Yildiz has just signed a new four-year deal and sources indicate that Juventus are unwilling to sell him.Atletico Bilbao winger Nico Williams is another who has been looked at before by Arsenal and would add some spark to an attack which can be criticised as being too predictable at times.The Spain winger has a contract until 2035 with the Basque club but there are reports which suggest there is a release clause in his contract.Williams completed 43.8% of his 153 dribbles last season, scored six goals and registered three assists in a campaign that was disrupted by injury.According to Opta, Williams averaged 8.2 dribbles per 90 minutes last season in La Liga with only Lamine Yamal, Kevin and Jeremy Doku averaging more in Europe's top five leagues.Availability is a big thing for Arteta and with a potentially high price tag and after a season of broken game time, this may not be the player for the Gunners at this point.Arsenal also have the option of continuing with Tzolis on the left while they also have Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke who can fill that role too, with Eze playing from the left in some of Arsenal's biggest games at the business end of last season.Arsenal are going to start the season with half of their first-choice back four out injured which means that any defender they sign is going to be required to play straight away.That is why the Gunners have been interested in a move for Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa who, as well as being a reliable centre-back, can play at right-back too.Konsa has become a starting option for England and, alongside his importance to Villa, that will be why he is valued at around £60m.However, Konsa is not the only defender that Arsenal have on their shortlist of targets.The Gunners are interested in a move for Cristian Romero who is the captain of their rivals Tottenham Hotspur.If any move does materialise for Romero, it would be a sensational development and be another deal, following the one for Eze last season, which would present a chance for bragging rights for Arsenal fans.Atletico Madrid are reported to be chasing Romero though and with Spurs unlikely to want to strengthen their rivals, this deal seems unlikely to come to fruition.

title: European Athletics Championships 2026: Amy Hunt wins 100m gold for GB
description: Amy Hunt had her coming of age moment as she stormed to 100m glory to claim her first senior international title and deliver Britain's first gold meda
body: Amy Hunt had her coming of age moment as she stormed to 100m glory to claim her first senior international title and deliver Britain's first gold medal of the European Athletics Championships.Hunt announced herself on the sport's global stage last year with world 200m silver in Tokyo - the first individual international medal of her senior career.Having backed that up with Commonwealth 100m silver two weeks ago, the 24-year-old would not be denied gold this time in Birmingham."I have had such a string of silvers and I was starting to get a bit fed up with it, so I thought it was time for gold," Hunt, who won in 11 seconds flat, told BBC Sport."My parents gifted me these gold earrings to finally level up, because I wear all-silver jewellery. "They said it was time for gold - they left me that note two nights ago - so it made me quite emotional."It was definitely time for me to come of age here."It was Britain's second medal on the opening day of action after the hosts took silver in the mixed 4x400m relay.Yemi Mary John held off Dutch athlete Myrte van der Schoot on the home straight to bring a British quartet also featuring Ben Jefferies, Charlotte Henrich and Toby Harries home in three minutes 10.47 seconds, behind winners Norway (3:09.62).Hunt's breakthrough individual medal last September was a long time coming, but the early years of her senior career were disrupted by injury as she sought to balance the demands of training with studying for an English Literature degree at Cambridge University.Before those challenging years, Hunt set a women's under-18 200m world record in 2019 - breaking Asher-Smith's British under-20 record in the process - but it would be six years before she managed to improve on that personal best time in her favoured event.Hunt also ruptured her quad muscle in 2022 but, with those setbacks now behind her, continues to make exciting progress under the guidance of coach Marco Airale in Italy's northern city of Padova.Now consistently able to produce personal-best performances, the silverware is beginning to follow - and this golden moment signalled a changing of the guard at the top of British sprinting.Discussing her ambitions before the championships, Hunt quoted High School Musical character Sharpay Evans, who sings a song called "I Want It All" in the film.Full of confidence after breaking the 11-second barrier for the first time earlier this season, she raised her arms in celebration after producing a trademark strong finish which delivered her from fifth to first over the second half of the race."I want it all and I'm someone who doesn't shy away from what she knows she can do," said Hunt."I knew I could come away with gold. I had such a big premonition."Hunt could have as many as three opportunities to add to her tally this week, as se competes in the 200m and both the women's and mixed 4x100m relay events.Typically not the quickest off the blocks at almost six-foot tall, Hunt was seventh in the eight-athlete final after the first 10m.But she held her form superbly to overhaul her rivals and end her wait for gold, just two years after finishing seventh in the previous European final in Rome."I just had such a magical feeling," Hunt said."I've won English Schools here, raced here as a 13, 14-year-old. I just had a feeling that this was going to be my night."My first gold. I think it was definitely time for an upgrade, and I'm now kind of fully established."British record holder Asher-Smith lined up in Birmingham as the defending champion - but the 30-year-old could not force her way into medal contention.Asher-Smith, bidding to win a historic seventh gold and become the joint-most successful athlete in the history of the championships, finished fifth in 11.10, as Poland's Ewa Swoboda (11.02) and Belgian Delphine Nkansa (11.06) completed the podium.Like Hunt, Asher-Smith will have further opportunities to draw level with Croatian discus thrower Sandra Elkasevic and Norway's Jakob Ingebrigtsen, who earlier won a superb 5,000m gold on his comeback from injury.Both will return to action on Wednesday, when attention turns to the women's 200m medals before the weekend's relays.

schema.headline: European Athletics Championships 2026: Amy Hunt wins 100m gold for GB

title: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots
description: President Donald Trump has signed an order that calls for fewer childhood vaccines and also recommends splitting the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR)
body: President Donald Trump has signed an order that calls for fewer childhood vaccines and also recommends splitting the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR) shots."Decades ago, children received only a small fraction of the vaccines required today," Trump said on Monday. "In those times, people were much healthier and of course the high rates of autism now observed did not exist."The president has long cast doubt on the safety of MMR vaccines, but multiple studies have found no connection between the shots and autism.The order also recommends that the number of childhood vaccines drop to 11 from the existing 18 recommended by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP).Speaking in the Oval Office, Trump said that his administration "is recognising gold standard childhood vaccine recommendations for only 11 core vaccinations against the most serious and dangerous diseases".The immunisations recommended for all children under the order are for measles, mumps, rubella, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, Haemophilus influenzae type B, pneumococcal disease, human papillomavirus, and varicella or chicken pox."We're reducing them," Trump said. "It's not only that you're doing fewer vaccines, or jabs, as they say, but you're doing them in a series of visits to the doctor."The president suggested that the MMR vaccine could be "quite lethal" if given at once. He compared it to pouring a bottle of soda into a child's body.Experts say that allowing time between jabs means children are more likely to contract diseases in the interim or that they are more likely to miss appointments if there are multiple shots.According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, external (CDC), there is "no published scientific evidence that shows any benefit in separating the combination MMR vaccine into three individual shots". The agency says "most people who get MMR vaccine do not have any serious problems with it", and that getting the vaccine "is much safer than getting measles, mumps, or rubella".Trump's Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F Kennedy Jr said the proposed changes were meant to give parents choice, not prohibit access to childhood vaccines.The federal government does not have the authority to implement the new recommendations. Shots that are required for school attendance are set at the state level.Dr Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics, called Trump's executive order "disheartening" and "dangerous", pointing out it comes as measles cases reach a 35-year high in the US. Measles cases have also been rising globally. "Instead of ensuring every family can access life-saving vaccines for measles, influenza, RSV and more, federal leaders are once again spreading misleading claims," Racine said in a statement on Monday.He said there was no new evidence to justify the significant changes, adding that the order was not based on "gold-standard science"."Delaying or skipping shots is risky, especially as measles continues to spread and children go back to school," Racine said. Republican Senator Bill Cassidy also admonished Trump's executive order on Monday, labelling it "wrong"."The President does not have the expertise to make these changes," Cassidy, who is a physician, wrote on social media. "Vaccines are overwhelmingly safe. Vaccines are effective. Vaccines DO NOT cause autism."The lawmaker, who chairs the Senate health committee, urged parents to "listen to their child's pediatrician about vaccines rather than listening to an inaccurate executive order". Experts fear that if parents refrain from getting their children vaccinated as a result of the discredited idea that childhood vaccines are linked to autism, it risks the re-emergence of diseases like measles.Multiple studies have found no link between the MMR vaccine and autism. A recent high-quality study from Denmark in 2019 looked at 657,461 children and concluded that the data did not support the MMR vaccine causing or triggering autism.On its website, the US CDC recommends that two doses of the combined MMR vaccine be given to children, starting with the first dose at 12-15 months and the second between the ages of four and six.How often and how many vaccines children in the US receive is based on the times when vaccines will work best with their immune systems and when they are most vulnerable to certain diseases, according to the AAP.There is no medical reason to delay or skip recommended immunisations, the AAP says.

schema.headline: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots

title: At least 111 killed in Colombia's largest  earthquake in years
description: The epicentre of the quake was near the village of San José del Palmar, in Chocó province, but local mayor León Fabio Marín Moncada said that there ha
body: The epicentre of the quake was near the village of San José del Palmar, in Chocó province, but local mayor León Fabio Marín Moncada said that there had miraculously been no deaths or injuries - despite the roads in and out being damaged. About 55km (34 miles) from the epicenter of the earthquake, the city of Pereira saw some of the worst damage. Videos verified by the BBC show at least one building collapsing in Plaza Bolívar, the city's main square, with scattered debris and dust across the open space where many people had gathered.Local authorities have reported at least 40 people dead in the city's metropolitan area, with 65 collapsed buildings. People are believed to be trapped in 15 of them. A curfew is in place in some parts of the city until 05:00 local time on Tuesday. Thirty-two buildings collapsed in Cali, located about 160km south of Pereira and about 200km from the epicentre.  Dan Cutler, 29, is from London but has been in Colombia for about two months as part of a big trip with his partner, and is currently in Cali. Being woken by the earthquake, he told the BBC:  "I've never experienced anything like it.""We sprinted outside in our pyjamas. There's no major structural damage to the hotel, but there are surface cracks in the walls, and paint and plaster have peeled off," he says.There were also reports of deaths in Manizales, Quibdó, Medellín, across the Chocó and Valle del Cauca regions.At least two people have died in Manizales.Speaking to BBC World Service, Angélica Ávila said she had been staying in a hotel in Manizales. She said as the earthquake hit, cracks appeared in the walls. "Everyone was screaming... I saw dust coming out of the neighbouring buildings, and bricks were falling off the walls," she said.Journalist and meteorologist Luis Felipe Molina, from Manizales, was at home when the earthquake struck - about 150km from the epicentre. He explained that due to previous earthquakes, the city has "very strict seismic-resistant building regulations" - so his building was able to resist the impact. "I have 450 books and only a few were left standing on the shelves. You could hear glass breaking and people screaming," he told BBC Mundo. "It was a terrible and terrifying experience."The country's aviation authority has reported damage at several regional airports, including those in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura.In the capital, Bogotá, trees and traffic lights shook violently, with reports of cracks in buildings but so far none of any serious damage to the city's infrastructure. Tremors were felt as far away as  neighbouring Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama. The quake comes less than two months after twin quakes devastated the north of Venezuela, killing more than 6,300 people.Colombia's President Abelardo de la Espriella has declared a national disaster situation, creating special powers to react to the emergency, including to reallocate budgets. Having only taken up the role on Friday, the new president is immediately faced with a potentially legacy-defining event. Along with the dead, he confirmed that more than 1,500 homes had been damaged.   As the extent of the damage has begun to emerge, world leaders have come forward to offer support. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it was "closely monitoring" the earthquake, and stood "ready to support", while EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said the EU's Copernicus satellite was being used in the rescue operation. The President of El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, sent a message of solidarity to the Colombian people and offered personnel and equipment for rescue efforts.According to the US Geological Survey, an estimated 1.5 million people felt shaking close to magnitude seven.It stated that deep earthquakes, like the one which hit on Monday, are usually less dangerous than earthquakes which break closer to the Earth's surface. But they can release energy in a way which is damaging to buildings, with fewer but potentially stronger aftershocks.

schema.headline: At least 111 killed in Colombia's largest  earthquake in years

title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
description: New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to stop betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving hig
body: New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to stop betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and "for many people, the high streets they grew up with have become unrecognisable".BBC News has exposed organised crime on high streets across the country, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes and vapes, selling cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".The plans announced by the government include:Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco or up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least £1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.Burnham said "the rise of vape shops, betting shops and rogue operators have replaced the shops, services, and community spaces that people are crying out for".He added: "That's not on. I said we would improve Britain's high streets, and that's exactly what we are starting to do."We're putting communities back in control and giving local people a real say over what opens on their high street."In response to the announcement, Conservative shadow communities secretary Sir James Cleverly said "once-treasured shops" have been replaced by a "smattering of rogue operators".But Sir James said increases to business rates by Labour had left "empty units for whoever is left standing to fill".He said: "Unless the government takes steps to support the high streets and hard-working businesses, Labour's increases in planning regulation will just mean more empty and boarded up shops."For the Liberal Democrats, home affairs spokesman Max Wilkinson said Burnham's plan "could go up in a puff of smoke" unless he toughens up powers to "properly crack down on cowboy vape shops and dodgy operators".His calls included asking the prime minister to scrap the business rates system.Reform UK economy spokesman Robert Jenrick said: "Until this government scraps the jobs tax, addresses sky-high business rates and provides real, fundamental support for high street businesses, this policy will only create even more empty shops on our high streets."A Green Party spokesperson said the government's proposals "look like more inadequate tinkering and reannouncements".They called on the prime minister to "go further and allow councils to introduce rent controls for small businesses". The Betting and Gaming Council said it supports "tough action against criminal operator" and agrees "local people should have a proper say over their high streets".A spokesperson for the industry body added it was "simply wrong" to suggest that betting shops are spreading "unchecked", adding around 3,000 shops have closed since 2019.Councillor Eamonn O'Brien, who chairs the Local Government Association, said it was "positive" that councils and communities "will get a greater say on what shops and services are found on their high streets".For 18 months, BBC News has reported on high street organised crime, including drug gangs, money laundering, child sexual exploitation reports, immigration crime and ghost directors linked to shop fronts selling illegal cigarettes and illegal vapes.In April 2025, the BBC joined the NCA as it raided barbers, mini-marts and vape shops in response to growing intelligence reports that some of these shops were being used for money laundering and illegal working.In May and June of last year, the team found secret underground tunnels supplying sacks of illegal cigarettes to high street mini-marts in Hull.In July last year, mass Freedom of Information requests revealed for the first time that 3,700 illegal shops had operated across the UK.In November, the BBC exposed asylum seekers buying and selling high street mini-marts for cash and criminal kingpins erasing £60,000 illegal working fines, and revealed a Kurdish organised crime gang operating on high streets the length of Britain.In response, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood launched an "urgent" investigation led by the NCA, Immigration Enforcement, HMRC and police forces from across the country. She said the BBC's evidence proved that "the system was broken" and demonstrated a pull factor in the small boat crisis.In March the BBC revealed a senior council worker had repeatedly shared with West Midlands authorities reports of children as young as 11 being sexually abused in high street mini-marts, and last month undercover reports exposed how cocaine, cannabis, laughing gas and prescription pills were being offered for sale.One street visited in the West Midlands was described as "lawless" by an anonymous law enforcement source.After the report, six mini-marts and vape shops on one high street in Cradely Heath, Sandwell were forced to close following an investigation by police and Trading Standards.Earlier this year, ministers announced a £30m enforcement operation targeting high street businesses suspected of money laundering, tax evasion and illegal working. Raids involving police, HMRC, Trading Standards and Immigration Enforcement have since taken place across the country.Additional reporting by Phill Edwards and Richard Wheeler

schema.headline: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces

title: More than two-thirds of England now in drought
description: Chair of the National Drought Group, Tony Grayling, said that drought conditions will continue to worsen until "significant and sustained rainfall".Th
body: Chair of the National Drought Group, Tony Grayling, said that drought conditions will continue to worsen until "significant and sustained rainfall".The week ahead is forecast to remain mostly dry, as the fifth heatwave of the year intensifies, although there are signs of some rain coming into the UK on Sunday."We know the hot and dry weather is taking a real toll on farming and there will be long-lasting impacts on our environment," Grayling said in a statement, adding that "we need everyone's help in using a little less water to make sure our current water reserves last".The National Drought Group said most of England is now experiencing a flash drought, which "develops very quickly" and is "brought about by a combination of very low rainfall and higher temperatures."Yorkshire and north-east England have been moved to "prolonged dry weather" status, which is the stage before drought. Nowhere in England is now under a "normal" status. Hot weather is continuing, with the UK Health Security Agency issuing amber heat health alerts for all of England apart from the North East from Tuesday at 09:00 BST until Friday at 21:00 BST. An amber alert means significant impacts "are likely" across health and social care services due to the high temperatures.The continued hot and dry conditions increase the risk of wildfires. Dozens of firefighters are currently battling a fire in the New Forest, which earlier on Monday was estimated to be the size of 140 football pitches (247 acres). Scotland and Northern Ireland have not been experiencing drought conditions and are expected to see spells of heavy rain over the week ahead.Scotland does not declare drought, but monitors "water scarcity".While conditions have improved in some parts of Scotland following recent rainfall, some eastern areas remain in the two most extreme categories of "moderate" or "significant" scarcity, according to the Scottish Environment Protection Agency.Last month, England and Wales saw the driest July since records began in 1836 - while for southern England, it was the driest month ever recorded.South-east England received 1% of the expected average rainfall for July, while some parts of Hampshire, Isle of Wight and West Sussex have not had a rain day for 59 days.All of England is experiencing pressure on water resources, the National Drought Group said.Farmers have reported reduced output after their earliest harvests in 20 years, with the National Farmers Union (NFU) warning that continued dry weather could lead to some food shortages.NFU president Tom Bradshaw said yields of wheat and oats were "very, very poor" this year and warned livestock farmers have had to use their winter feed rations because they have been unable to grow grass.Water Minister Emma Hardy said the government is working to make it easier for farmers to build more on-site irrigation reservoirs, which capture and hold water.Vegetables to get smaller and more expensive due to hot weather, farmers warnOnly 14% of England's rivers are considered to be at normal levels, while 22% are "exceptionally low" - including the River Avon in south-west England and the River Ely Ouse in eastern England.The Environment Agency has warned that low water levels have resulted in potential navigation issues for boats on the Thames, Lark and Ouse.Reservoir levels have also continued to decline, with almost all across England below normal and five classed as "exceptionally low", according to the agency.Warmer water is putting fish under "severe stress," Head of Fisheries at the Angling Trust Mark Owen said, as it holds less dissolved oxygen.Emma Pinchbeck, chief executive of the Climate Change Committee, said the UK is "not prepared at all" for the prolonged dry weather."We're seeing right now with the impacts on farming from this drought and the extreme heat we're experiencing, our infrastructure, our agricultural sector and lots of areas of the economy are not really ready for the weather we now have and how that weather will change up to 2050," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.What has been striking about this summer is not any single record, but the way weather extremes are piling up.Climate change does not cause every heatwave or drought, but it does shift the odds.By raising average temperatures, it makes extreme heat more likely and, when rain fails, increases evaporation and dries soils faster. That creates a feedback - dry ground cools the air less, allowing temperatures to climb still higher.The UK is now seeing the kind of hotter, drier summers climate scientists have long projected, part of a global pattern of heat.  There have been three droughts in the past five years – in 2022, 2025 and now 2026.This year, there have been 34 days with temperatures that have reached 30C or above somewhere in England, including 13 consecutive days in July. Heat extremes are becoming more likely and more intense due to human-caused climate change, the Met Office says.Meanwhile, El Niño - the recurring climate pattern in which unusually warm Pacific Ocean waters can affect weather around the world - is giving global temperatures an additional, natural boost.  The World Meteorological Organisation, the UN agency for climate and weather, says a strong El Niño event is developing and is expected to "dominate global climate patterns" in the coming months.

schema.headline: More than two-thirds of England now in drought

title: Jeff Bezos & Liverpool: Consortium including American advances talks
description: A consortium including billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has advanced its talks to buy about a 30% stake in Liverpool, BBC Sport has been told.The
body: A consortium including billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has advanced its talks to buy about a 30% stake in Liverpool, BBC Sport has been told.The group is led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia and also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.Owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) confirmed last month that the group had "expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club".Bhatia is the son-in-law of Indian billionaire businessman Lakshmi Mittal and had been a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers for 18 years before relinquishing his stake in the club last month.American businessman Bezos, founder of e-commerce giant Amazon, is the fourth-richest person in the world.According to Forbes, the 62-year-old has an estimated net worth of $256bn (£192bn).FSG, who bought Liverpool in a £300m deal in 2010, previously sold a minority stake in the Anfield side to global sports investment firm Dynasty Equity. BBC Sport contacted FSG about the latest developments, but they had no further comment.In January, Liverpool became the top-earning Premier League club for the first time, according to analysis from financial firm Deloitte. The following month the club announced record revenues of £703m for 2024-25 financial year.

schema.headline: Jeff Bezos & Liverpool: Consortium including American advances talks

title: The Cambridge University lecturer who kept her Tourette's secret
description: 'I felt Tourette's would ruin my life, now I teach at Cambridge'Image caption, Throughout her academic life, Dr Amanda Cole has kept her Tourette's hi
body: 'I felt Tourette's would ruin my life, now I teach at Cambridge'Image caption, Throughout her academic life, Dr Amanda Cole has kept her Tourette's hidden - until nowByLaurence CawleyEast InvestigationsDr Amanda Cole was 15 and sitting in a religious studies class when she experienced a peculiar spasm at the back of throat. She assumed it would pass, but it was a vocal tic and her first known manifestation of her Tourette's syndrome, a condition that causes people to make sudden, repetitive sounds or movements."How am I going to have a family? How am I going to have a job?" Cole, 32, remembers asking herself as she lay awake at night after her diagnosis in her 20s at her home on the Debden Estate near Loughton, Essex. "I thought it was going to destroy my life."Now a married mother-of-one, Cole is an assistant professor in sociolinguistics at Cambridge University, but throughout her academic life she has kept her Tourette's hidden - until now.Following an incident at this year's Bafta Film Awards ceremony in which a guest shouted out offensive words because of his tics, Cole said she wanted to be open about her condition and allowed the BBC to join her as she began telling colleagues and students.Image source, Cole familyImage caption, When growing up, Cole did not tell friends or classmates about her Tourette's"I felt so scared of Tourette's," says Cole, who is one of about 300,000 people in the UK living with the condition. "There was no-one I knew that had Tourette's, and I didn't see anyone in the public eye that had Tourette's - and if they did, they were a figure of ridicule. "The only impression I had of Tourette's was people acting... and they were swearing, and they were shouting, and they were being obnoxious."As a result, she hid the condition from friends growing up and colleagues by either by suppressing the tics or releasing them when the person she was speaking with looked away.Even now, Cole says she retains "some residual shame" about her condition and wants to live in a world where people can "tic freely" without embarrassment. "It's quite liberating telling people, whether it's students or friends because most of the time people are just like 'oh, OK, fine'," says Cole, who is also autistic.The most recent data from the Higher Education Statistics Agency, external shows out of about 245,000 academic staff working in the UK's institutions, just 70 - or 0.03% - have disclosed a developmental condition that affects motor or cognitive skills.Experts believe the true number may be far highe, externalr and that many academics with conditions such as Tourette's hide their neurodiversity for fear of repercussions.Cole's vocal tics tend to include the names of her husband, her son or the family cat or random phrases such as "good night" during the day time."I worry a little bit [that] I'm like the palatable face of Tourette's  - I don't swear, I don't say anything that is going to be too challenging."I think what we just really need as society is an understanding of Tourette's, an understanding of tics and to know that tics aren't what we really think," she says.The words are merely "a neurological event that we have no control over", she adds.Emma McNally, the chief executive at Tourette's Action, says many of those with coprolalia end up self-isolating from society.She adds that many people with Tourette's find people accepting of their condition until they say something that feels as though "it's about them"."People then take offence even though there's no malice behind it," says McNally. While Cole and many others with Tourette's have developed often very sophisticated strategies to mask their tics, not everybody can suppress them, McNally says.But unreleased tics need to come out at some point, Cole says, and storing them up is physically uncomfortable - she describes the sensation as akin to an "itch" or "suppressing a sneeze". When she is alone, she will then spend time releasing all of those suppressed tics - a process that can take a few minutes."I've gone to great lengths at times to hide my Tourette's," she says. "Some people with Tourette's can't suppress at all, and some people can suppress to a lesser or greater degree."Women, she says, tend to be more adept at "masking" the condition.Image caption, After giving a morning lecture about accents, Cole joined students Tim Morrice (left) and Abbie Lovewell for a supervision sessionThe BBC joined Cole in May for her first lecture in which every student was aware of her Tourette's."I had no idea until she told us," says linguistic student Tim Morrice. "But I really appreciate her telling us because I think it's really nice to see neurodivergent people in academia because it isn't a thing we see or hear very much."Fellow student Abbie Lovewell says finding out about Cole's Tourette's made absolutely "no difference" to her or how she views her supervisor."I think she's one of the best supervisors that I've had," she adds. 'Productive superpowers'When asked if she would take a magic pill that removed her Tourette's, Cole responds with a firm "no"."I wouldn't ever want to get rid of my Tourette's because my brain is wired the way my brain is wired, and I like being me and the people that love me, like me being me."Tourette's, she says, can also offer a selection of "superpowers"."I really have hyperfocus - something that has been well-documented as part of Tourette's," she says, describing being able to spend hours on a task she has set herself such as research, painting or playing the piano. "I can really, really focus and be really, really, really productive," she says.Image caption, Cole's husband, Ed Wellington, says he did not realise his wife had Tourette's at firstHowever, there can be disadvantages to Cole's hyperfocus, according to her husband Ed Wellington, such as getting her attention when she is involved in a task or her refusal to stop doing household tasks in spite of the time, once she has begun.Her tics and her Tourette's in general, however, have never been something the pair have really discussed, he says."From when I first met her, I could sort of tell she had something about her - she had real energy and drive," says Wellington. "I didn't know she had Tourette's. I didn't know that for quite some time."He describes making various small adjustments to prevent Cole being "overwhelmed" by sensory stimuli, such as leaving the room to eat crisps because the crunching sound feels like it is coming through a "megaphone right into her ear"."If she's feeling really over-stimulated I have to like go around like turning off all the main lights," he says. "I have to Tourette-proof the room for her a bit."Image caption, Cole says she feels her teenage self "would be well happy if she could see me now"Owing to Tourette's often being genetic, Cole says if her son develops the condition she will encourage to him to "harness" its "huge strengths". "I know any mother is going to say this, but he is going to be wonderful because he is already wonderful." When asked what she would say to her frightened 15-year-old self, Cole says: "You're going to be fine, you don't need to be scared, Tourette's is fine."I don't feel I've lived my life despite my Tourette's, I feel I've lived my life well with Tourette's and autism. It has really helped me achieve and made me the person I am."I think my teenage self would be well happy if she could see me now."
